title: CI interpreter coverage and shard timing
summary: Full CI and change-scoped selections default explicitly to Ubuntu 26.04; server-image jobs remain on Ubuntu 24.04 pending their own upgrade proof. The shared runner action declares postgresql-client-16, installs missing host clients from PGDG only on GitHub-hosted runners, and refuses self-hosted runners with ci_runner_prerequisites_missing and package recovery. CI installs no embedded-engine libraries, so fresh hosts prove product portability. Runner upgrades require full CI on both Python endpoints. The separate Check runner capacity step measures the median of three Python loops before Run pytest. Values above 0.05 seconds refuse as ci_runner_slow with measured value, limit and recovery, retained in pytest-output.txt. When only capacity failed, item-owned rerun-failed permits failed-job recovery within three total attempts; pytest or other step failures still refuse ci_rerun_verdict. Setup precedes admission; later host degradation remains outside this check. The pytest step uses PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1. Required shard-coverage jobs compare each interpreter leg with an independent unsplit collection after scope deselection, refusing missing reports and missing, duplicated or unexpected test IDs. Reused suites skip this check. One collect-only pass records fixture and marker facts in parallel with wheel building, then publishes deterministic per-scope file groups balanced by recorded file weights. Shards reuse the existing pre-import collection filter with all suite-root conftest anchors, retain assigned file lists and worker collection counts/ID hashes, and never split after collection. Unknown files receive mean file weight; product-wheel files stay together. Parameter IDs remain stable across runner patch versions.
